name: Titanium.UI.Animation
summary: The `Animation` object defines an animation that can be applied to a view.
description:
An animation object describes the properties of an animation. At its most basic, an animation
object represents a single-phase animation with an end state and a duration.

When [animate](api:Titanium.UI.View#animate) is called on a [View](api:Titanium.UI.View), the view is
animated from its current state to the state described by the animation object. The properties
that can be animated include the view's position, size, colors, transformation matrix and opacity.

You can also specify an animation curve or *easing function* to control the pace of the
animation. To use an easing function, set the animation's `curve` property to one of the
`ANIMATION_CURVE` constants defined in [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI). For example,
[ANIMATION_CURVE_EASE_IN](api:Titanium.UI#ANIMATION_CURVE_EASE_IN) specifies an animation that
starts slowly and then speeds up.

Animations can be set to reverse themselves automatically on completion, and to repeat a given
number of times. For more complicated effects, multiple animations can be combined in sequence,
starting one animation when the previous animation completes.

Use the [Titanium.UI.createAnimation](api:Titanium.UI#createAnimation) method to create an animation object.

Note that on SDKs older than 9.1.0, when you animate a view's size or position the actual layout properties (such as
`top`, `left`, `width`, `height`) are not changed by the animation. See the description of the
[animate](api:Titanium.UI.View#animate) method for more information.

As of 9.1.0, the animated properties should reflect their final values just before the `complete` event and/or the [Ti.UI.View.animate](api:Titanium.UI.View#animate) callback is fired.

#### iOS Platform Notes

iOS supports both 2D and 3D matrix transformations in animations.

iOS also supports *transitions* between windows or views. You can create a transition
by creating an animation object and setting the `view` property to the view you want to
transition to. The `transition` property specifies the transition effect to apply. Use one of
the transition style constants defined in [Titanium.UI.iOS.AnimationStyle](api:Titanium.UI.iOS.AnimationStyle).

#### Android Platform Notes

Android supports 2D matrix transformations. Note that the
[Matrix2D.rotate](api:Titanium.UI.Matrix2D#rotate) method operates differently on Android. Called
with a single argument, it rotates from zero to the specified angle. That is, it ignores any
existing rotation. Called with two arguments, it interprets the first argument as a "from"
angle and the second argument as a "to" angle.

properties.name: anchorPoint
properties.summary: Coordinate of the view about which to pivot an animation.
properties.description:
Used on Android only. For iOS, use [Titanium.UI.View.anchorPoint](api:Titanium.UI.View#anchorPoint).

Anchor point is specified as a fraction of the view's size.  For example, `{0, 0}` is at
the view's top-left corner, `{0.5, 0.5}` at its center and `{1, 1}` at its bottom-right
corner.

This property's value will overwrite the [anchorPoint](api:Matrix2DCreationDict#anchorPoint) used in the matrix's creation dictionary.

See the "Using an anchorPoint" example for a demonstration.

properties.name: autoreverse
properties.summary: Specifies if the animation should be replayed in reverse upon completion.

properties.name: backgroundColor
properties.summary:
Value of the `backgroundColor` property at the end of the animation, as a color name
or hex triplet.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: bottom
properties.summary: Value of the `bottom` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: bounce
properties.summary: The animation bounce. If set, the animation uses the iOS 17+ spring animation.
properties.description:
When `bounce` is 0, there are no bounces, positive values indicate increasing amounts of bounciness up to a maximum
of 1.0 (corresponding to undamped oscillation), and negative values indicate overdamped springs with a minimum value of -1.0.

properties.name: center
properties.summary: Value of the `center` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: color
properties.summary: Value of the `color` property at the end of the animation, as a color name or hex triplet.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: curve
properties.summary: Animation curve or easing function to apply to the animation.

properties.name: dampingRatio
properties.summary: The damping ratio for the spring animation as it approaches its quiescent state.
properties.description:
Use a value between 0 and 1. For a smoother deceleration use values closer to 1.
To increase oscillation use value closer to 0.

properties.name: delay
properties.summary: Delay, in milliseconds before starting the animation.

properties.name: duration
properties.summary: Duration of the animation, in milliseconds.

properties.name: elevation
properties.summary: Value of the `elevation` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: height
properties.summary: Value of the `height` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: left
properties.summary: Value of the `left` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: opacity
properties.summary: Value of the `opacity` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: opaque
properties.summary: Value of the `opaque` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: repeat
properties.summary: Number of times the animation should be performed.
properties.description:
If `autoreverse` is `true`, then one repeat of the animation consists of the animation
being played once forward, and once backward.

properties.name: right
properties.summary: Value of the `right` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: rotationX
properties.summary: Value of the `rotationX` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: rotationY
properties.summary: Value of the `rotationY` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: springVelocity
properties.summary: The initial spring velocity.
properties.description:
For smooth start to the animation, match this value to the velocity of view as it was prior to attachment.
A value of 1 corresponds to the total animation distance traversed in one second.
For example, if the total animation distance is 200 points and you want the start of the
animation to match a view velocity of 100 pt/s, use a value of 0.5.

properties.name: top
properties.summary: Value of the `top` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: transform
properties.summary: Animate the view from its current transform to the specified transform.
properties.description:
Over the course of the animation, the view interpolates from its current transform to the
specified transform.

3D transforms are only supported on iOS.

properties.name: transition
properties.summary: Transition type to use during a transition animation.
properties.description:
The new view being transitioned to **should NOT** be a child of another view or
of the animating view. The animation replaces the current view from the
view hierarchy and adds the new view to it.

properties.name: view
properties.summary: New view to transition to.
properties.description:
Specify the `transition` property with one of the transition style constants defined
in [Titanium.UI.iOS.AnimationStyle](api:Titanium.UI.iOS.AnimationStyle) to select the effect to apply.

The new view being transitioned to **should NOT** be a child of another view or
of the animating view. The animation replaces the current view from the
view hierarchy and adds the new view to it.

properties.name: visible
properties.summary: Value of the `visible` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: width
properties.summary: Value of the `width` property at the end of the animation.

properties.name: zIndex
properties.summary: Value of the `zIndex` property at the end of the animation.
properties.description: Refer to [Titanium.UI.View.zIndex](api:Titanium.UI.View#zIndex) for an explanation of z-index.

events.name: cancel
events.summary: Fired when the animation is canceled.
